description: Major mountain ranges, their heights, locations, and geological significance

overview.formation: Mountains form through tectonic plate collisions (fold mountains), volcanic activity, or block faulting
overview.fourteen_eight_thousanders: 14 peaks above 8,000 m; all in Himalaya/Karakoram

himalayas.location: South Asia; Nepal, India, Bhutan, Tibet, Pakistan
himalayas.formation: India-Eurasian plate collision; 50 million years ago; still rising
himalayas.significance: Water tower of Asia; 14 rivers originate here

karakoram.characteristics: More glaciers than anywhere outside polar regions

andes.location: South America; Venezuela to Tierra del Fuego
andes.formation: Nazca plate subducting under South American plate

rocky_mountains.location: Western North America; Alaska to New Mexico
rocky_mountains.significance: Continental Divide; watershed between Pacific and Atlantic drainage

alps.location: Central Europe; France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, Germany, Slovenia
alps.cultural: Source of Rhine, Rhône, Danube, Po; skiing, tourism; influenced European history

caucasus.location: Between Black Sea and Caspian Sea; Russia, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan
caucasus.highest: Mount Elbrus: 5,642 m (highest in Europe by some definitions)

urals.location: Russia; traditional boundary between Europe and Asia

great_dividing_range.significance: Separates coastal from inland Australia; headwaters of Murray-Darling

seven_summits.europe: Elbrus - 5,642 m (or Mont Blanc - 4,808 m depending on definition)
seven_summits.australia_oceania: Puncak Jaya - 4,884 m (Papua, Indonesia) or Kosciuszko

mountaineering_history.first_everest: Edmund Hillary (NZ) and Tenzing Norgay (Nepal); May 29, 1953
mountaineering_history.k2_winter: First winter ascent January 16, 2021; Nepali team
